sources.citation: Fields, Philip C. 1991. A phonology of the Orya language. Papers in Papuan Linguistics 1 (Pacific Linguistics A-73).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Nearest published phonology within Tor-Orya (Orya is the sister branch); useful only as a family-level comparandum, not a Kwinsu source.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Alison J. Robinson (eds.). 2026. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 29th ed. Dallas: SIL Global. Free page for Kwinsu [kuc].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitted by Randy Lebold, SIL). 2007. Request for Change to ISO 639-3 Language Code, Change Request Number 2007-233: create [kuc] Kwinsu. 8 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology or stress. Only states that an SIL survey in August 2005 found the variety spoken at Ansudu village to be a distinct Tor language on wordlist comparison, and cites 'Survey Report on the Kwanem Languages. Draft survey report.' as its sole source.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page for Kwinsu (kwin1242), and Tor-Orya family page (toro1256)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No descriptive reference at all for Kwinsu: only Lee & Wambaliau 2004 and Ethnologue 2025. Family-level refs (Ross 2005, Fields 1991 Orya phonology, Voorhoeve 1975, Smits & Voorhoeve 1994) do not cover Kwinsu.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Kwinsu language' (stub) and 'Orya–Tor languages'; Wikipedia (id) has no 'Bahasa Kwinsu' page
sources.note: Nothing; stub cites only Ethnologue. Tor family page cites Foley 2018 for classification only.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of Northwest New Guinea. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 433-568. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no library e-access found (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Only modern descriptive overview of the Tor-Orya family (phonology sketches drawn mainly from Berik/Orya); may give family-level generalisations on stress that would apply to Kwinsu by inheritance, but nothing Kwinsu-specific is expected.

sources.citation: Lee, Sang-Kem & Theresia Wambaliau. 2004 [survey Aug 2005]. Kwanem languages survey report in Northeastern Papua, Indonesia. Draft SIL Indonesia survey report, 88 pp. (Glottolog 140386)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only primary work on Kwinsu; a sociolinguistic survey with wordlists for Ansudu and the other Coastal Tor villages. Wordlist transcriptions might carry stress marks or a phonological note; it is the sole possible statement on Kwinsu stress. Unpublished; held by SIL Indonesia / SIL Language & Culture Archives (search pages blocked from here).
